decision: The general normal-kernel recognition theorem is valid for arbitrary groups and a finite family of normal subgroups. Both written presentation applications discharge its hypotheses and recover the exact stated earlier clauses. The note removes the final finite-order comparisons from these presentation arguments. It neither replaces all of F016 nor establishes a new source count, conjecture answer, or compression ratio.

written_results.reason: Off-diagonal coordinate triviality and faithfulness on each local subgroup give pairwise trivial intersections. Normality then makes the subgroups commute. Coordinate projection detects every factor of a product, so multiplication is an internal direct-product identification. Base-kernel containment puts any joint-kernel element in that product. A surjection through which the actual coordinates factor is therefore injective. No candidate-group finiteness, cardinality equality, or desired global injectivity is assumed. The empty indexing family also satisfies the assertion.

The complete local presentations give maps E_S to P_S. Composition with the constructed quotient and the S-coordinate is the identity on the local generators, proving local injectivity without counting. Distinct antichain supports meet properly, so a local kernel has trivial image in every other coordinate by the corresponding proper-subgroup faithfulness. The exact base presentation after killing all local kernels identifies the base kernel with their join. Theorem 1 then applies. UA.SK proves generation of the whole compatible product, not merely its generated subgroup's inclusion in an ambient product. Additional deletion and geometry conclusions retain their separate hypotheses.

written_results.primary_read: arXiv:1901.09034v1, physical pp. 7-9, exact Theorem 3.2 and its complete proof; the already retained square decomposition was checked in canonical UA.
checks: The defining involutions, three pair powers, three normality relators, and parity word agree with the primary presentation after renaming markers.

With rightmost-first affine multiplication and [x,y]=x^-1 y^-1 x y, the parity words are translations (0,-2) and (-2,-2). Their signed-permutation orbits generate the stated square or diagonal lattice for every parameter; this is an exact normal-closure argument.

Each marked dihedral quotient is faithful on its proper marked subgroups. Its kernel is inverted by its two local generators and centralized by the remaining generator. All three kernels are therefore normal in the candidate group.

The parity commutators vanish in every pair coordinate after deletion. Killing the three kernel words leaves exactly the complete affine-square presentation with the appropriate parity relation; the larger original pair powers become redundant.

The resulting order and pair orders follow after the isomorphism. The extension dot does not assert splitting. The square or diagonal quotient decompositions use UA.SquareDecomposition, with dihedral subscripts denoting group order.

The regular hypertope conclusion uses the base flag property and UA.SK.Geometry, not intersection property alone. The square base has the required property through the retained regular-polytope correspondence.

written_results.primary_read: arXiv:2512.15511v1, equation (8) on physical p. 6, Theorem 5.1 and its iterated construction on pp. 8-10, complete Theorem 5.3 proof on pp. 11-12.
checks: Each local square quotient H_n to H_5 is faithful on every proper marked subgroup, because all marked pair orders remain 4,4,2. Its entire third lower-central subgroup is used; the false independence of the two squared translation subgroups is not assumed.

The binary vertex/edge coordinate model is a complete class-two path presentation. Every path vertex and edge occurs in a consecutive triple, so projection from the compatible product to all local factors is injective. Its generators are exactly the source's iterated mix tuples, proving equality of marked constructions rather than equality merely of order and section types.

The four-marker calculation is valid: with x=bab and F=(cd)^2, commutation with ax and a gives [x,F]=1; [x,d]=1 then gives [cxc,d]=1. Both factors of (cbab)^2 commute with d, and conjugating the inverse by b gives the second word. Reversal covers the other nearest outside generator; more distant generators commute by the string relations.

The extra four-marker commutator holds in the class-two base and in every triple coordinate, since one of its two disjoint pairs loses a generator there. Thus the proposed presentation maps to the actual compatible product.

After killing the local third lower-central subgroups, all adjacent squares are central. The residual presentation and the class-two path base map onto each other by the same generators, and the compositions fix all generators. This proves the exact base quotient without a finite-order upper bound.

The unquotiented group P0 has all deletion maps: the even Coxeter relators and the complete square-lattice relators survive deletion. UA.D gives intersection property even if P0 is infinite. Its local groups embed through the faithful maps onward to H. The complete defining presentation and retained string C-group/polytope correspondence give the asserted universality.
When d=3, there is one local triple and no four-marker relator, as required. Boundary triples for higher d need only the available nearest outside generator.
corrections_preserved: In H6 the two doubled translations coincide as a nonidentity element of order two; the source's independence assertion in its proof is not repeated.

The note does not reprove all flatness, flat amalgamation property, alternating semiregular, or other F016 conclusions. Identifying its constructed group with the source's mix does not turn this note into a complete replacement of the paper.
